\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বাড়া} (bāṛā)}{বাড়া (bāṛā)}]{\bn{বাড়া} (bāṛā) — to grow; to go up (in amount)}

\label{lesson:BN-C372-bara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to supply, then the Bengali for a limit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বাড়া}}
\textbf{\bn{বাড়া}} — \emph{bāṛā} — \textquotedblleft{}to grow; to go up (in amount)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দাম} \bn{বাড়লে} \bn{লোকে} \bn{কম} \bn{কেনে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dām bāṛle loke kôm kene.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When prices go up, people buy less.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{নদীর} \bn{জল} \bn{বাড়ল}, \emph{sei nôdīr jôl bāṛlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বাড়া}} (\emph{bāṛā}) is a tadbhava of Sanskrit \emph{várdhatē}, grows (CDIAL 11376 lists Bengali bāṛā). It is the partner of the taught \bn{বাড়ানো}: prices \bn{বাড়ে} by themselves; someone \bn{বাড়ায়} them.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāṛā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāṛā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dām bāṛle loke kôm kene.} — When prices go up, people buy less.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to supply, then the Bengali for a limit, then say \emph{bāṛā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বাড়া} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To grow; to go up (in amount)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কমা} (kômā)}{কমা (kômā)}]{\bn{কমা} (kômā) — to fall; to decrease}

\label{lesson:BN-C372-koma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a limit, then the Bengali for to grow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কমা}}
\textbf{\bn{কমা}} — \emph{kômā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fall; to decrease\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জ্বর} \bn{না} \bn{কমলে} \bn{ডাক্তার} \bn{ডাকো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jbôr nā kômle ḍāktār ḍāko.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the fever doesn't come down, call a doctor.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{জ্বর} \bn{কমল}, \emph{sei jbôr kômlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কমা}} (\emph{kômā}) is a Bengali verb made on \bn{কম}, less, usually traced to Persian \emph{kam}. It is the partner of the taught \bn{কমানো}: a fever \bn{কমে} by itself; medicine \bn{কমায়} it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kômā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kômā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jbôr nā kômle ḍāktār ḍāko.} — If the fever doesn't come down, call a doctor.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a limit, then the Bengali for to grow, then say \emph{kômā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কমা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To fall; to decrease\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দ্বিগুণ} (dvigun)}{দ্বিগুণ (dvigun)}]{\bn{দ্বিগুণ} (dvigun) — double; twice as much}

\label{lesson:BN-C372-dvigun}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to grow, then the Bengali for to decrease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দ্বিগুণ}}
\textbf{\bn{দ্বিগুণ}} — \emph{dvigun} — \textquotedblleft{}double; twice as much\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাতে} \bn{গেলে} \bn{ভাড়া} \bn{দ্বিগুণ} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāte gele bhāṛā dvigun hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you go at night, the fare will be double.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দ্বিগুণ}} (\emph{dvigun}) is Sanskrit \emph{dviguṇa}, \emph{dvi} 'two' with \emph{guṇa} 'a fold': twofold (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dvigun}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dvigun}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāte gele bhāṛā dvigun hôbe.} — If you go at night, the fare will be double.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to grow, then the Bengali for to decrease, then say \emph{dvigun} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{দ্বিগুণ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Double; twice as much\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{স্তর} (stôr)}{স্তর (stôr)}]{\bn{স্তর} (stôr) — a level; a layer}

\label{lesson:BN-C372-stor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to decrease, then the Bengali for twice as much.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{স্তর}}
\textbf{\bn{স্তর}} — \emph{stôr} — \textquotedblleft{}a level; a layer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বৃষ্টির} \bn{পরে} \bn{নদীর} \bn{জলের} \bn{স্তর} \bn{অনেক} \bn{বাড়ল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{brishṭir pôre nôdīr jôler stôr ônek bāṛlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the rain the water level in the river rose a lot.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{স্তর}} (\emph{stôr}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{stara}, 'a layer' (CDIAL 13685). In modern use a layer of something has also become its level: \bn{জলের} \bn{স্তর}, the water level.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{stôr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{stôr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{brishṭir pôre nôdīr jôler stôr ônek bāṛlô.} — After the rain the water level in the river rose a lot.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to decrease, then the Bengali for twice as much, then say \emph{stôr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{স্তর} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A level; a layer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পরিমাণ} (pôrimān)}{পরিমাণ (pôrimān)}]{\bn{পরিমাণ} (pôrimān) — an amount; a quantity}

\label{lesson:BN-C372-poriman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for twice as much, then the Bengali for a level.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পরিমাণ}}
\textbf{\bn{পরিমাণ}} — \emph{pôrimān} — \textquotedblleft{}an amount; a quantity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জলের} \bn{পরিমাণ} \bn{কমলে} \bn{গাছ} \bn{শুকিয়ে} \bn{যাবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jôler pôrimān kômle gāchh shukiye jābe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the amount of water drops, the plants will dry up.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পরিমাণ}} (\emph{pôrimān}) is Sanskrit \emph{parimāṇa}, a measure all round, a quantity (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrimān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrimān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôler pôrimān kômle gāchh shukiye jābe.} — If the amount of water drops, the plants will dry up.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for twice as much, then the Bengali for a level, then say \emph{pôrimān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পরিমাণ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An amount; a quantity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
